text:
Toronto played the better game and lost by three. The Maple Leafs held the edge in expected goals, 3.31 to 2.67, and a simulated replay of every shot gives them the win 68 percent of the time. The gap came down to goaltending. Ilya Sorokin stopped 28 of 29 shots for the Islanders against 3.31 expected goals, saving 2.31 goals more than the chances deserved. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed three on 19 shots, 0.71 goals worse than expected.

The Islanders cashed their chances while Toronto's mostly died. Anthony Duclair scored on an 11 percent look at 8:18 of the first, and Bo Horvat made it 2-0 late in the second on a 26 percent wrist shot. Colton Sissons cut it to 2-1 early in the third with a 7 percent tip-in, and Toronto outchanced New York 1.39 to 0.69 in the period. The best look of the night, a 37 percent chance for Nick Paul in the first, missed the net. Toronto also went 0 for 3 on the power play despite 0.83 expected goals.

Simon Holmstrom ended it with two goals in the final four minutes. His first, at 14:08, came on a 55 percent chance with assists from Horvat and Matthew Schaefer. His second, at 17:55, was unassisted on a 38 percent look. Horvat took first star with a goal and an assist, and Sorokin was the third star. Toronto won the first meeting of the season 2-1 on Sept. 30.
